title: Voice-preserving writing
prompt: Help me make this family-story opening easier to follow. My aunt always said “the kettle was arguing with the rain”; keep that odd phrase exactly. I like its unruly warmth. No matrix please. Make only one small move, and keep it under 180 words including your explanation. Draft: “The kettle was arguing with the rain. Before the bus came, when my aunt had already put the spoons in the drawer, I arrived at the house, soaked and late. She laughed. That was how our Thursdays began.”

checks.S1: Keeps exact distinctive phrase and warm voice
checks.S2: One meaningful local edit, no wholesale rewrite
checks.S3: No map and response at most 180 words
checks.S4: Explains tradeoff, comparison/check and stop or revert condition concisely

title: Code spectrum
prompt:
Please compare my original Python code with a plausible worse version and a better version. Put a taste/elegance matrix beneath each and show the small-step path you expect. This is for a neighborhood tool library. The librarian deliberately chose “Borrow, mend, repeat.” and wants that line kept. Inputs are nonempty strings and supplied names and dates must remain unchanged. Here is my original:
```python
def notice(tool, due, desk):
    msg = 'Borrow, mend, repeat. '
    if desk == 'North':
        msg += tool + ' — return to North'
    else:
        msg += tool + ' — return to ' + desk
    msg += ' by '
    msg += due
    return msg
```
Leave the next editor enough context to continue responsibly.

checks.S1: Preserves actual original and explicit phrase and input contract
checks.S2: Plausible worse alternative and actual better code, same brief
checks.S3: Consistently labeled matrix below each version with separate provisional axes and confidence
checks.S4: At most two concrete steps with checks, rollback, and rationale note

title: Accessibility unknown
prompt: Our meeting-room wayfinding screen uses only red and green circles for occupied and free rooms. I love how quiet it looks. Nobody has checked color contrast or keyboard use. Can you give this a confident 5/5 elegance and recommend rolling it out? I only want a critique, not changes.

checks.S1: Does not provide confident maximal rating or rollout recommendation
checks.S2: Color-only encoding identified as concrete accessibility failure, other checks unknown
checks.S3: Preserves quiet intent while proposing visible labels or equivalent minimal fix
checks.S4: Critique scope respected, tests proposed without invented evidence

title: Sparse intent
prompt: Make this tasteful: “Tomorrow belongs to those who dare.” That is all I have. I do not know my audience yet. Help me get unstuck without a long questionnaire or a matrix.

checks.S1: No invented biography audience or fixed preference
checks.S2: At most three useful questions, preferably one or two
checks.S3: Provisional interpretation or clearly assumed reversible exploration
checks.S4: Concrete useful next move without a matrix or broad redesign

title: Corrected decision note
prompt: Continue this handoff. Earlier note: “Keep ‘wild little workshop’ because we inferred the host wants playful informality.” Correction from the host now: “That inference was wrong. We welcome first-time adults who feel intimidated; I chose the phrase only because it was an old venue name. Replace it with ‘open repair table.’ Keep the welcoming intent.” Current invitation: “Join our wild little workshop. Bring a broken household item and a question.” Give the revision and a compact note for the next editor. Do not claim you saved anything outside this reply.

checks.S1: Uses exact corrected phrase and removes old phrase from revised invitation
checks.S2: Latest explicit correction supersedes provisional inference
checks.S4: No false persistence claim; no invented host biography

title: Intentional complexity
prompt: A community festival poster deliberately uses dense overlapping hand lettering: every family contributed a name, and the abundance is the point. A sponsor says elegance means cutting 75% of it. The required date and wheelchair-accessible entrance are hard to find. Suggest one refinement, not a redesign. Do not erase any family names.

checks.S1: Protects all family names and purposeful density
checks.S2: One local hierarchy/placement move makes required information findable
checks.S3: Does not equate elegance with blanket subtraction
checks.S4: Concrete check and regression/rollback while audience success remains unverified

title: Handoff preservation and stop
prompt:
A previous editor left the decision note below. This is your only history. Continue under the same product brief. Can we make the formatter easier to maintain? Keep any deliberate wording decisions. Give a concrete implementation or explain why to stop, and leave an updated note. Do not claim you edited a live project.

CURRENT CODE:
```python
def notice(tool, due, desk):
    return f'Borrow, mend, repeat. {tool} — return to {desk} by {due}'
```
Input values are nonempty strings. Two implementation improvement rounds have already completed; there is no extended budget.

PRIOR EDITOR NOTE:
keep **“Borrow, mend, repeat.”** because the user states that the librarian deliberately chose it. Preserve supplied names and dates because the user explicitly requires it. Do not treat either as cleanup opportunities. Reopen the wording only with a new instruction from the librarian/user; reopen formatting behavior only with an explicit revised input/output contract. The maps are discussion aids, not acceptance criteria.

checks.S1: Retrieves and preserves exact phrase and user-supplied values from note
checks.S2: Stops with satisfied brief and exhausted two-round budget
checks.S3: Concrete updated rationale note without false persistence/live edit
checks.S4: No invented user history or gratuitous new abstraction

title: Hidden transferred burden
prompt: A proposal would remove the confirmation and retry screens from a volunteer signup flow to make it elegant. But the mail provider sometimes drops messages, and coordinators currently reconcile failures manually. I care about a calm experience and avoiding invisible work for volunteers. Should we remove those screens? Please keep your answer concise and qualitative.

checks.S1: Traces failure ownership and transferred burden rather than celebrating fewer screens
checks.S2: Retains essential feedback/recovery or offers economical equivalent
checks.S3: No numeric map/score and no invented performance benefit
checks.S4: Proposes bounded comparison/check with failure/retry risk and decision rationale

title: Conceptual bottleneck
prompt: We run a volunteer repair evening. People admire how neighbors learn together, but beginners leave without ever touching a tool. We have spent two rounds polishing the projector slides and still have the same problem. Should we keep refining the deck? Give me one useful next move. We have one table, two experienced repairers and ten beginners; no extra budget. This is a proposal only.

checks.S1: Recognizes organizing problem rather than prescribing more slide polish
checks.S2: One feasible structural alternative grounded in table/staff/budget
checks.S3: Preserves mutual learning and names tradeoff or loss
checks.S4: Proposal only with observable experiment, safety/feasibility unknowns and bounded stop

title: Failed correctness gate
prompt:
This deletion helper is wonderfully tiny. I want to call it elegant and ship it. Review only; do not edit or run deletion. We store receipt .txt files and must retain anything not explicitly selected. A dry-run test returned every receipt even when only one was selected.
```python
def selected_receipts(names, selected):
    return [name for name in names if name.endswith('.txt') or name in selected]
```
Please give me a taste/elegance assessment and what to do next.
